data.narrative:
Quantum Machines is a Series C quantum computing company that has raised $280M to date. The quantum computing sector comprises 11 identified peers—3 public (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private companies including Quantinuum, IonQ, D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Infleqtion.

The valuation analysis relies on a stage-progression methodology, which is applicable but operates in isolation. This method applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the $280M total capital raised as a proxy for current value, yielding an implied valuation of $476M. A peer-median approach is not viable; while 6 same-sector peers exist, insufficient datapoints meet narrow filters (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or comparable valuation tier) to generate reliable medians, and a broad all-sector median would lack fidelity.

The single-method analysis supports a valuation range of $405M to $547M, centered on $476M. The median estimate reflects the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties stem from the absence of tight peer comparables in quantum computing—a nascent sector with heterogeneous technical approaches and commercialization timelines—and reliance on a single quantitative method. Revenue or unit economics data, if available, would strengthen conviction in this range. Until additional comparables mature or the company's operational metrics become available, this range should be treated as preliminary and revisited upon material developments.
